reasons: No tests are visible in this file.
Many JSON and text fields rely on comments rather than checks.
Dates are stored as a mix of text and real dates.
Two budget fields use different number types, which could cause confusion.

terms.meaning: The written description of the database tables, their columns and their rules.
An extra lookup structure that makes searching a table faster.
A rule that a value in one table must match an existing row in another table.
A rule that stops two rows from having the same value or combination of values.
A library that checks that data has the right shape before it is saved.
A text format for structured data, stored here in columns that accept more complex values.
Copied exactly word for word from the original source.
A named checkpoint a project must pass to show it is mature enough to proceed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the main schema
sections.what: Brings in the column types, the schema validation helper and the zod library needed to define the main tables.
sections.why: These tables cannot be defined without these imports.

sections.name: projects (part 1)
sections.title: Main project record
sections.what: Stores one row per project with its name, description, budgets, role, megawatts, industry, status, dates, costs, parties, supply chain, variances and many other facts.
sections.why: Reason not stated for every field. The core project table is the anchor that the other tables link to.
sections.watch_out: Two budget fields use different number types, so comparing them directly can give rounding surprises.

sections.name: projects (part 2)
sections.title: Indexes for project search
sections.what: Adds indexes that speed up searches and sorts on the main project fields, such as status, lifecycle stage, maturity, country, industry and key dates.
sections.why: Likely reason: the project list and filter pages search on these fields.
sections.watch_out: Each extra index makes writes to the table a little slower.

sections.name: evidenceQuotes
sections.title: Evidence quotes behind project facts
sections.what: Stores exact quotes from sources that support project facts, with the URL, publisher, date, the field each one supports, and whether it is still active. It also records how the quote is anchored and which validation rule accepted it.
sections.why: The comments explain that these fields exist for traceability and for the verbatim check.
sections.watch_out: The provenance class is empty for all existing rows, so code that reads it must handle null.

sections.name: issues
sections.title: Issues per project stage
sections.what: Records problems for a project at a lifecycle stage, with their impact, a description and a list of evidence references.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The evidence references are strings that the database does not check against real evidence.

sections.name: scorecardPillars
sections.title: Scorecard pillars
sections.what: Stores scorecard categories for each project, with a score, trend, confidence, positives, negatives, evidence references and SKU matches.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the field names.
sections.watch_out: The SKU matches field accepts any shape, so its contents are not checked at compile time.

sections.name: maturityGates
sections.title: Maturity gate status per project
sections.what: Stores one status for each maturity gate of each project, with a score contribution, a rationale, the verbatim quote behind it, its source, a confidence level and a link to the evidence row.
sections.why: The comments say a verbatim quote is required for any status other than unknown, so each claim can be traced.
sections.watch_out: The verbatim requirement is only a comment. The verbatim column accepts empty values in the database.

sections.name: successStories
sections.title: Success story per project
sections.what: Stores a short list of facts and takeaways for each project, with one story per project.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: glossaryTerms
sections.title: Glossary terms by industry
sections.what: Stores glossary terms and definitions for each industry, each with a list of supporting citations including optional locator details.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the table and field names.
sections.watch_out: The citation shape is defined inline and is not enforced by the database.

sections.name: milestones
sections.title: Project milestones
sections.what: Stores the key steps of a project with a planned date, an actual date and a status.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The status is free text, so the database does not limit it to a set list.

sections.name: projectUpdates
sections.title: Dated project updates
sections.what: Stores news or update items about a project, with a date, a headline, the source, a link, an excerpt and a locator. The source publication time is always set, but the event date may be empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps updates tied to projects and sortable by date.
sections.watch_out: Sorting by event date and by publication time can give different orders, since the event date may be empty.

sections.name: technologyDetails
sections.title: Technology details per project
sections.what: Stores reactor and capacity details for a project, with one row per project.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The fields suggest they describe reactor projects.
sections.watch_out: The table allows only one row per project, so a second set of details for the same project will be rejected.

sections.name: skuMappings
sections.title: SKU mappings per project
sections.what: Stores how well a project item matches a category, with a description and an alignment score.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: No allowed range for the alignment score is enforced in this table definition.

sections.name: researchJobs
sections.title: Research jobs for projects
sections.what: Tracks each background research job for a project, with its trigger, who started it, status, timing, error, retry count and the maximum retries, which is 3 by default. It also stores the verbatim check report for the run.
sections.why: Likely reason: the retry fields let a failed job try again later. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: Only one queued or running job is allowed per project, and the status values in SQL are uppercase, so the status text must match exactly.

sections.name: researchJobSteps
sections.title: Log of each research step
sections.what: Records each step of a research job, including how many attempts were made, its status, start and finish times, and any error. The app can use this to show progress and to see which step failed.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps a history of research steps so a failed step can be retried without losing what happened before.
sections.watch_out: The status column is free text, so a misspelled status name is not caught by the database.

sections.name: researchJobDocuments
sections.title: Web pages collected for research
sections.what: Stores each web page a research job gathered for a project, with its address, domain, trust tier, title, and a short snippet. This is the record of which sources were used.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps findings traceable back to the pages they came from.
sections.watch_out: The address is required, so a source without an address cannot be saved.

sections.name: realityScanRuns
sections.title: Saved Reality Scan runs
sections.what: Holds one row for each Reality Scan run, with the chosen scope, the resolved mode (enrich, scratch, or mixed), overall status, current stage, and any error.
sections.why: The comments say run state must survive restarts and that the mode is recorded honestly rather than forced into one value.
sections.watch_out: The mode is empty until the resolve_mode stage has run, so early rows will have no mode.

sections.name: realityScanStageResults
sections.title: Results for each scan stage
sections.what: Holds the outcome of each named stage in a Reality Scan run, with one row per stage.
sections.why: The comment says a resumed run updates the existing row for that stage instead of adding a duplicate.
sections.watch_out: Each run can have only one row per stage, so changing that unique rule would break resuming.

sections.name: lessonsLearntRuns
sections.title: Saved Lessons Learnt runs
sections.what: Holds one row per Lessons Learnt run. Besides the scope and status, it records how many projects were in scope versus processed, whether a cap cut the list short, and the path and checksum of the generated slide file.
sections.why: The coverage fields exist so the output does not overstate how complete the analysis was.
sections.watch_out: The artifact path points to a file on disk. If that file is removed, this row still exists and will point to nothing.

sections.name: lessonsLearntStageResults
sections.title: Stage results for Lessons Learnt
sections.what: Holds one row per stage of a Lessons Learnt run, following the same pattern as the Reality Scan stage table.
sections.why: The code states it uses the same durability pattern as Reality Scan.
sections.watch_out: The one-row-per-stage rule applies here too.

sections.name: lessonsLearntPillars
sections.title: Pillars of the lessons recipe
sections.what: Stores each pillar (a main theme) of a Lessons Learnt run, with counts of facts, projects, strengths and risks, and the decision on whether a risk rule was applied and why.
sections.why: Likely reason: the recipe used to live only inside a slide file, and this table makes it queryable.
sections.watch_out: The risk decision and its reason are required, so every pillar must record why its risk rule was or was not applied.

sections.name: lessonsLearntDrivers
sections.title: Drivers under each pillar
sections.what: Stores each driver, a named cluster of related lessons, under a pillar. It keeps the name, the reasoning, whether the name came from a model or a fallback, and any review flags.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the named clusters and their reasoning so they can be reused and reviewed.
sections.watch_out: A comment lists three allowed values for the naming field, but the database accepts any text.

sections.name: lessonsLearntDriverFacts
sections.title: Links drivers to supporting evidence
sections.what: Connects each driver to the evidence quotes that back it, kept in a set order.
sections.why: The comment says every evidence id must point to a real evidence quote, which makes this the audit trail for each driver.
sections.watch_out: An id that does not match an existing evidence quote is refused, so the write fails rather than saving an empty link.

sections.name: lessonsLearntCoverage
sections.title: Ledger of items a run considered
sections.what: Holds one row for each item a Lessons Learnt run looked at, recording whether it was admitted into the output, why it was held back if not, and which slides cite it.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows which sources actually made it into the final deck and which did not.
sections.watch_out: Run, item kind, and item id together must be unique, so writing the same item twice in one run will conflict.

sections.name: yardRunRecords
sections.title: Stored outputs from tool runs
sections.what: Holds the outputs of tool runs against Yard projects, one row per value. Conflicting values are all kept, each with its source.
sections.why: The comment says conflicts are kept rather than hidden, so a reader can see the disagreement.
sections.watch_out: Values are stored as text, so numbers and dates must be converted before any calculation.

sections.name: changeLog
sections.title: History of project field changes
sections.what: Records every change made to a project field, who made it, the old and new values, and where the value came from. An undone change stays in the log and is marked reverted.
sections.why: The comment says undoing marks a change as reverted rather than deleting it, so the history stays complete.
sections.watch_out: The review state defaults to approved, so a new change is accepted unless the writer sets another state.

sections.name: schedules
sections.title: Recurring check timing per project
sections.what: Stores how often a project should be checked again, the time zone, the preferred time of day, and when it last and next ran.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app quickly find checks that are due, using an index on enabled schedules.
sections.watch_out: Each project can have only one schedule, because the project id is unique.

sections.name: companies
sections.title: Company records
sections.what: Stores a company's name, type, country, website, description, headquarters, founding year, and industry.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the fields themselves.
sections.watch_out: The type column is free text in the database even though a fixed list of allowed types exists elsewhere in this file.

sections.name: companySources
sections.title: Web addresses to check for a company
sections.what: Stores web addresses linked to a company, with the source type, how often to check it, when it was last checked, and whether it is switched on.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app keep a list of pages to monitor for each company.
sections.watch_out: Sources are enabled by default, so new addresses are checked automatically.

sections.name: companyAliases
sections.title: Other names for companies
sections.what: Holds alternate names a company is known by, so searches can match them.
sections.why: Likely reason: company names vary across sources, so aliases help matching.
sections.watch_out: The same alias cannot appear twice for one company.

sections.name: companyProjectLinks
sections.title: Links between companies and projects
sections.what: Records that a company has a given role on a project, with a confidence score and the first and last times that link was seen.
sections.why: Likely reason: captures roles discovered from sources over time.
sections.watch_out: A company can hold the same role on the same project only once.

sections.name: discoveryJobs
sections.title: Log of company discovery runs
sections.what: Records each automatic search for new projects or updates, with its status, timing, and a summary of what it found.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app report what each discovery run did.
sections.watch_out: The summary is optional, so any report that reads it must handle a missing value.

sections.name: sources
sections.title: Catalogue of information sources
sections.what: Lists the sources the app can use, each with a trust tier (defaulting to 3), category, region, industry, and whether it is enabled.
sections.why: Likely reason: the trust tier lets the app prefer more reliable sources.
sections.watch_out: The id is supplied by the writer rather than generated, so a duplicate id will conflict.

sections.name: projectSources
sections.title: Links projects to sources
sections.what: Simple pairs that connect a project to a source.
sections.why: Likely reason: records which sources feed each project.
sections.watch_out: There is no uniqueness rule here, so the same pair can be stored twice.

sections.name: aiSynthesisCache, insertProjectSchema, insertEvidenceQuoteSchema, insertIssueSchema
sections.title: Cached AI summaries and form checks
sections.what: Stores AI-written synthesis results for an industry along with an expiry time, so they are not regenerated every time. This section also builds the validation rules for inserting rows into most tables.
sections.why: The comment says the cache id is the same key the in-memory cache uses, so one lookup finds either copy.
sections.watch_out: Expired rows remain in the table, so any read must check the expiry time itself.

sections.name: insertAiSynthesisCacheSchema
sections.title: Validation rule for cache rows
sections.what: Validation for cache rows that keeps the id field, because the caller supplies the cache key.
sections.why: The comment explains that the id is not auto-generated, so it is deliberately not removed.
sections.watch_out: If the id were removed from this rule, the cache key would be lost on insert.

sections.name: realityScanScopeSchema, RealityScanScope
sections.title: Rules for a scan's scope input
sections.what: Defines the shape of the scope a user picks for a scan, covering research options, peers, industries, segments, projects, and companies.
sections.why: The comment says the schema checks shape only, and the routes enforce that at least one selection is made.
sections.watch_out: An empty selection passes this rule, so the route that receives it must reject it.

sections.name: insertRealityScanRunSchema, insertRealityScanStageResultSchema, Project, InsertProject
sections.title: Validation rules and type names for projects and scans
sections.what: Builds validation rules for new scan runs and stage results, and gives short type names for each table so other code can use them.
sections.why: Likely reason: avoids repeating table definitions across the app.
sections.watch_out: The id and timestamp fields are removed from the run rule, so the database must fill them in.

sections.name: InsertRealityScanStageResult, LessonsLearntScope
sections.title: Shared scope type for lessons
sections.what: Makes Lessons Learnt use the same scope rules as Reality Scan.
sections.why: The comment says both use the same shared scope resolver.
sections.watch_out: A change to the scan scope rules also changes Lessons Learnt.

sections.name: insertLessonsLearntRunSchema
sections.title: Validation rule for Lessons Learnt runs
sections.what: Validation for new Lessons Learnt runs, leaving out the id and timestamp fields.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, though it matches the Reality Scan pattern.
sections.watch_out: None clear from this section.

sections.name: insertLessonsLearntStageResultSchema, LessonsLearntRun, InsertLessonsLearntRun, LessonsLearntStageResult
sections.title: Validation and type names for lesson stages
sections.what: Validation for lesson stage rows and short type names for the lesson run and stage tables.
sections.why: Likely reason: same reuse purpose as the other type sections.
sections.watch_out: None clear from this section.

sections.name: partiesSchema
sections.title: Check for a list of parties
sections.what: Checks a list where each entry has a role and a name, both required text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Empty text is rejected, but the role is not checked against any known list.

sections.name: supplyChainSchema
sections.title: Check for a supply chain list
sections.what: Checks a list of components, each with a supplier and a status, all as text.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Empty strings pass this check.

sections.name: variancesSchema
sections.title: Check for cost and schedule variance
sections.what: Checks cost and schedule variance data: planned and actual values, the change, the reason, and the delay in months. The whole value may be empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: records how far a project moved away from its plan.
sections.watch_out: Once the data is present, every number is required, so partial data is refused.

sections.name: similarProjectsSchema
sections.title: Check for similar projects list
sections.what: Checks a list of similar projects, each with an id, a name, and the reason it matched.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The list has no maximum length.

sections.name: citationLocatorSchema
sections.title: Check for where a quote sits
sections.what: Checks a pointer to a location in a source, such as a text fragment, a PDF page, or an anchor.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader jump to the exact passage.
sections.watch_out: The value is optional, so a locator with only a type passes.

sections.name: citationItemSchema, citationsSchema, CitationItem
sections.title: Check for citation entries
sections.what: Checks a citation with an id, title, and address, plus optional publisher, access date, excerpt, and locator.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each claim traceable to its source.
sections.watch_out: The address is only checked as text, not as a valid web address.

sections.name: COMPANY_TYPES
sections.title: Allowed company types
sections.what: The fixed list of company types the app accepts.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps type values consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: The database column does not enforce this list, so the two can drift apart.

sections.name: PROJECT_ROLES
sections.title: Allowed project roles
sections.what: The fixed list of roles a company can hold on a project, such as owner, operator, or EPC contractor.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps role values consistent.
sections.watch_out: A new role must also get a label in the next section.

sections.name: ROLE_LABELS
sections.title: Display names for roles
sections.what: Maps each role to a readable label and a short definition, so screens show plain names.
sections.why: Likely reason: users see labels rather than internal codes.
sections.watch_out: The map includes some types that are not in the project role list, so the two lists must be kept separate in use.

sections.name: compassCommentary
sections.title: Paraphrased Compass remarks
sections.what: Stores short paraphrased remarks from a person linked to a project, with a link to the source record.
sections.why: The comment says it keeps only paraphrases, never verbatim quotes, and that the table must not be dropped after an earlier incident.
sections.watch_out: The address field is required and this table must not be removed in a schema change.

sections.name: compassThemes
sections.title: Compass themes per project
sections.what: Stores named themes from Compass for a project, with takeaways and an optional link to a related remark.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Each row is unique per project, slot, and source record, so duplicates are refused.

sections.name: compassFindings
sections.title: Compass findings per project
sections.what: Stores each Compass finding with its wording, stance, confidence, and the evidence ids it rests on.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each finding tied to the evidence behind it.
sections.watch_out: The evidence ids are plain text in a list, and this table does not check that they exist.

sections.name: computationRecord
sections.title: Record of each calculation
sections.what: Logs each calculated value with the method name and version, its parameters, its inputs, and the evidence behind it.
sections.why: The comments explain that the run id has no link to a run table because it can point to two different tables.
sections.watch_out: The duplicate rule treats missing ids as equal, and a generated schema diff must not rewrite that rule.

sections.name: sourceDocument
sections.title: Stored source documents
sections.what: Holds a document's text or a pointer to where it is stored, along with title, publisher, fetch time, and for uploads, the file name, category, and confidentiality level.
sections.why: The comments say the upload time is kept apart from the fetch time so that an upload is never recorded as fetched.
sections.watch_out: The comment says text is stored inline or offloaded, but no rule here enforces that one of the two is set.

sections.name: sourceSpan
sections.title: Exact passages inside documents
sections.what: Pins a quote to an exact character range in a document, with a page or section label that a person can read.
sections.why: The comment says exact character positions are hard to read, so a page label is added.
sections.watch_out: The rule that the end must come after the start is in the SQL, not here, so code writing these rows must respect it.

sections.name: internalCommentary
sections.title: Internal remarks from people
sections.what: Stores a paraphrase of something a team member said about a project, with the date said, the channel, and the consent level.
sections.why: The comments say it differs from Compass remarks: the address is optional and the time spoken is kept separate from the time saved.
sections.watch_out: A paraphrase must never be shown as a direct quote, and the consent level must be respected when showing the person.

sections.name: forecastRecord
sections.title: Forecasts for project values
sections.what: Stores forecasts for a project's fields, with the as-of date, horizon, value, method, and confidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps predictions separate from measured values.
sections.watch_out: If the linked calculation or evidence is deleted, the forecast stays but loses that link.

sections.name: compassSyncLedger
sections.title: Log of Compass sync results
sections.what: Records each sync from Compass for a project and source record, with counts of findings and verified and conflicting items, plus the detailed ledger.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows how much of a sync was verified and where conflicts were flagged.
sections.watch_out: The ledger is required, so even an empty sync must supply a list.

summary: Defines the main tables of the app: projects and the research, scoring, lessons learnt, reality scan, company and compass records that hang off them.
purpose: Describes the main data the app stores about projects and the work done on them.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the overall split. Several comments explain individual fields, such as delayIsApproximate.
how: It imports the column types and the zod schema helper. It then defines the main projects table, followed by many related tables, each with its columns and indexes. Later sections define validation schemas and type names used by other code.
inputs: Not visible in this file. Rows are written by the research pipeline, the reality scan, the lessons learnt process and other code.
outputs: Table definitions, validation schemas and type names used by the rest of the app.
risks: Several JSON fields accept any shape at the database level. Some dates are plain text while others are real dates. There are two budget fields with different types.
debug: If a project field looks wrong, check whether it is text or a real date, since text dates are not validated by the database. If a new research job will not start, check whether one is already queued or running for that project, and check the uppercase status values.
